name: 46,XY Difference of Sex Development Due to Testicular Steroidogenesis Defect
aliases: 46,XY DSD due to steroidogenic enzyme deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Biochemical Diagnostic Criteria for 46,XY DSD due to Testicular Steroidogenesis Defect

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic variants in genes encoding testicular steroidogenic enzymes
Abnormal serum steroid hormone profile indicating impaired androgen synthesis (e.g., low testosterone, elevated precursor steroids)
Presence of undervirilized external genitalia or ambiguous genitalia in a 46,XY individual
Imaging evidence of testicular tissue with absence or hypoplasia of Wolffian structures
Positive family history of similar disorders or consanguinity

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical presentation with confirmatory biochemical profile and genetic confirmation of steroidogenic enzyme defect
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including endocrinology, genetics, and radiology.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Ambiguous external genitalia with micropenis or hypospadias
Low serum testosterone with elevated steroid precursors

common.symptomName: Delayed or incomplete virilization at puberty
Reduced muscle mass and body hair

occasional.symptomName: Psychosocial distress related to gender ambiguity
searchTerms: emotional problems due to ambiguous genitalia

rare.symptomName: Salt-wasting crisis due to associated adrenal steroidogenesis defects
searchTerms: adrenal hormone deficiency causing salt imbalance
high blood pressure from mineralocorticoid excess
blood pressure raised by adrenal hormones

rare.symptomName: Osteopenia or osteoporosis due to chronic hypogonadism
searchTerms: bone thinning due to hormone deficiency

laboratory: Elevated steroid precursors such as 17-hydroxyprogesterone or androstenedione
Abnormal LH and FSH levels indicating gonadal dysfunction
imaging: Ultrasound or MRI showing presence of testes with variable size and location
Absence or hypoplasia of Wolffian duct derivatives
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes such as HSD17B3, SRD5A2, CYP17A1, or STAR
other: Histopathology of gonadal tissue showing Leydig cell dysfunction

distinguishingFeatures: Normal or elevated testosterone with androgen receptor mutations
Normal testosterone with low dihydrotestosterone levels
Pathogenic variants in SRD5A2 gene specifically

redFlags: Ambiguous genitalia at birth in a 46,XY individual
Salt-wasting crisis or adrenal insufficiency symptoms
references: Hughes IA, et al. Consensus statement on management of intersex disorders. Arch Dis Child. 2006.
Ono M, et al. Molecular basis of 46,XY DSD due to steroidogenic defects. Endocr Dev. 2014.
Orphanet Report Series: 46,XY Difference of Sex Development due to Testicular Steroidogenesis Defect, ORPHA:90787
